title: Oppenheimer recalls the Trinity test and the Bhagavad Gita

tellings.quote: I remembered the line from the Hindu scripture, the Bhagavad Gita. Now I am become death, the destroyer of worlds.
Thou seest Me as Time who kills, Time who brings all to doom, The Slayer Time, Ancient of Days, come hither to consume;

plain: Watching the first atomic bomb test, at the Trinity site in New Mexico in 1945, the physicist J. Robert Oppenheimer recalls thinking of a line from the Hindu scripture the Bhagavad Gita: "Now I am become death, the destroyer of worlds." His own recorded words are played on the show. Oppenheimer does not say which translation he followed; in Edwin Arnold's 1885 English version, the god Krishna's words at that verse are "Thou seest Me as Time who kills, Time who brings all to doom."

discussion.by: The Song Celestial, or Bhagavad-Gita (translated by Edwin Arnold)
discussion.text: Oppenheimer does not say which translation his words follow (he read the Gita in Sanskrit); in Edwin Arnold's 1885 translation read here, Krishna's words at chapter 11, verse 32 are "Thou seest Me as Time who kills, Time who brings all to doom", not "Now I am become death, the destroyer of worlds".
